title: Crisis Escalation & Clinical Safety Review Pattern
description: A pattern combining pre-deployment clinical review of a chatbot's responses to crisis-adjacent input with a tested escalation path connecting the user to a trained human, so the chatbot never operates as an unsupervised substitute for crisis-capable human support.
problem: A chatbot tuned for general helpfulness can give responses that are actively harmful when a user is in psychological crisis or belongs to a vulnerable population (e.g. active eating-disorder symptoms, suicidal ideation), and without a tested escalation path, no human is positioned to intervene.
solution: Before deployment, have qualified clinicians review the chatbot's responses to a structured set of crisis-adjacent and vulnerable-population test inputs; build and test an escalation mechanism that reliably routes a user showing crisis indicators to a trained human responder; and treat any chatbot marketed to or known to reach a vulnerable population as requiring this review regardless of its original intended use case.
applicability: Any chatbot deployed in a mental-health-adjacent context, marketed as a companion or emotional-support product, or known to be used by minors or emotionally vulnerable individuals.
consequences: Clinical review requires access to qualified reviewers and is not a one-time exercise — it must be repeated as the underlying model changes; an escalation mechanism only helps if it is actually reachable and staffed, which is itself an ongoing operational commitment.

citations.title: Chatbot that offered bad advice for eating disorders taken down

relationships.reason: Tested clinical review and escalation is the concrete mechanism satisfying this control's reasonable-safeguards expectation.
The pattern's output is a crisis escalation protocol test report.
